# DSP Architecture: CORRUPTR

**CRITICAL CONTRACT:** This specification is immutable during Stages 1-4 implementation. Stage 1 Planning cannot proceed without this file. Stage 3 (DSP) implements this exact architecture.

**Generated by:** Stage 0 Research (research-planning-agent)
**Referenced by:** Stage 1 (Planning), Stage 3 (DSP Implementation)
**Purpose:** DSP specification defining processing components, signal flow, and JUCE module usage
**Complexity Tier:** 6 (DEEP research) — modular distortion/glitch/rhythm/modulation "playground" with 14 major subsystems
**Scope flag:** This MVP is substantially larger than a typical single-pass plugin. See `plan.md` for complexity score and phased-implementation recommendation. Do not treat this architecture as "implement in one sitting" — it is a multi-phase build.

---

## Scope Reconciliation Note (Brief vs. Draft Parameter Spec)

The creative brief describes a 12-stage signal chain (`PRE-EQ → DISTORTION → BITCRUSH/SRR → WAVEFOLDER/DIGITAL FX → GLITCH → RHYTHMIC GATE/STUTTER → FILTER → PITCH/FREQUENCY FX → STEREO → POST-EQ → MIX → OUTPUT/LIMITER`) as the **full long-term vision**. The MVP-scoped `parameter-spec-draft.md` implements a deliberately narrower slice of that vision:

- **Distortion is a single selectable algorithm** (`distortionAlgorithm` choice param cycling through all 12 types), not 12 simultaneous always-on stages. Wavefolder and Foldback are two of the 12 selectable algorithms, not a separate always-on "Wavefolder/Digital FX" module.
- **No separate Pre-EQ / Post-EQ pair** — MVP has one Filter stage (`filterType/filterCutoff/filterResonance`) positioned after Glitch, per the parameter spec's implied ordering. Pre/Post EQ as distinct stages is deferred.
- **"Rhythmic Gate/Stutter"** from the brief is absorbed into the Glitch Engine's `Stutter`/`Retrigger`/`Silence` modes plus the Sequencer's `Gate` modulation lane — not a separate gate module.
- **Pitch/Frequency FX and Stereo (Mid/Side, independent L/R)** are explicitly **post-MVP** per the brief's own scope note and are NOT in the draft parameter spec. Architecture below treats the signal path as mono-compatible dual-mono stereo (processed identically per channel except where LFO/mod-matrix stereo spread is explicitly called out for macroWidth).
- **Tape Stop/Tape Start** are NOT a separate "Tape/Mechanical FX" module (that whole section is post-MVP) — they are two of the 18 Glitch Engine modes, which IS in MVP scope.
- **Comb filtering** is delivered via `filterType = Comb`, not via the post-MVP "Micro Delay/Comb" module. The feedback-loop's internal delay line is a distinct, smaller, purpose-built element (see Feedback Routing below), not the general-purpose Micro Delay/Comb feature.

This reconciliation is the de facto MVP signal chain used throughout this document. Flag for confirmation during mockup finalization (Section 5 of the research protocol — no mockup exists yet, so this is a brief-vs-param-spec conflict rather than a mockup conflict).

## Core Components

### 1. Input Gain Stage
- **JUCE Class:** `juce::dsp::Gain<float>`
- **Purpose:** Gain-stage input signal before entering the processing chain.
- **Parameters Affected:** `inputGain`
- **Configuration:**
  - Range -24 to +24 dB, linear dB→gain conversion via `juce::Decibels::decibelsToGain()`
  - Smoothed via internal `juce::dsp::Gain` ramp (10-20ms) to avoid zipper noise on automation

---

### 2. Distortion Engine (12-Algorithm Waveshaper)
- **JUCE Class:** `juce::dsp::WaveShaper<float>` (per-algorithm transfer function) + `juce::dsp::Oscillator<float>` (Ring-Mod carrier) + `juce::dsp::DryWetMixer<float>` or manual smoothed-gain crossfade (stage mix)
- **Purpose:** Single selectable waveshaping algorithm (one active at a time) driven by Drive/Tone/Bias/Fold/Mix.
- **Parameters Affected:** `distortionAlgorithm`, `drive`, `tone`, `bias`, `fold`, `distortionMix`
- **Configuration:**
  - `drive` (0-40dB) → linear gain multiplier feeding the waveshaper input (`gain = dB2gain(drive)`)
  - `tone` (-100..+100) → one-pole tilt filter post-shaper (`juce::dsp::IIR::Filter` with `makeLowShelf`/`makeHighShelf`, or `juce::dsp::FirstOrderTPTFilter`)
  - `bias` (-100..+100) → DC offset applied pre-shaper for asymmetric clipping (Diode/Tube/Asymmetric character); offset removed post-shaper via a slow-moving DC blocker (`juce::dsp::IIR::Filter::makeHighPass` ~5Hz) to avoid DC creeping into downstream stages
  - `fold` (0-100%) → active only for Wavefolder/Foldback algorithms; controls number of fold-back iterations in the custom fold transfer function
  - `distortionMix` (0-100%) → per-stage dry/wet blend (distinct from master `mix`)
  - **Per-algorithm transfer functions** (all implemented as lambdas passed to `WaveShaper::functionToUse`, EXCEPT Ring-Mod which needs an oscillator, and Wavefolder/Foldback which need iterative folding logic beyond a single lambda but can still be expressed as a closed-form or short-loop function inside the lambda):
    | Algorithm | Function | JUCE support |
    |---|---|---|
    | Saturation | `tanh(gain*x)` | WaveShaper lambda |
    | Soft Clip | cubic/tanh soft-knee | WaveShaper lambda |
    | Hard Clip | `clamp(x, -1, 1)` | WaveShaper lambda |
    | Tube | asymmetric tanh w/ bias | WaveShaper lambda + bias offset |
    | Diode | piecewise exponential (diode I-V curve approximation) | WaveShaper lambda (custom exp curve) |
    | Fuzz | hard-clip cascaded with extra gain + odd-harmonic emphasis | WaveShaper lambda (2-stage) |
    | Digital Distortion | bitwise/quantized hard clip | WaveShaper lambda (reuses bitcrush quantizer at fixed depth) |
    | Bitcrusher | (see dedicated component #3) | N/A here — routed through component 3 when selected as "the" distortion voice isn't needed since Bitcrush is always-on separately; `distortionAlgorithm=Bitcrusher` choice is a UX convenience that also engages component #3 at a fixed reduced depth |
    | Sample Rate Reducer | see component #3 (same relationship as Bitcrusher above) |
    | Wavefolder | custom fold function: `x - 4*fold*round(x/4)` style triangle-fold | Custom (no JUCE class) |
    | Ring-Mod | `x * osc(carrierFreq)` | `juce::dsp::Oscillator<float>` sine carrier, freq mod-matrix destination |
    | Foldback | reflect-at-threshold recursive fold | Custom (no JUCE class) |
  - **Note:** `Bitcrusher`/`Sample Rate Reducer` as `distortionAlgorithm` choices create a coupling with the always-present Bitcrush/SRR stage (component #3). Recommend Stage 3 DSP implementation treat `distortionAlgorithm` as purely "which waveshaper curve is active" and leave Bitcrush/SRR entirely governed by their own always-on `bitDepth`/`sampleRateReduction` params, with the two "Bitcrusher"/"Sample Rate Reducer" choices in `distortionAlgorithm` simply being no-ops in the waveshaper (pass-through) since the actual crush/reduce happens in component #3 regardless of algorithm selection. **Flag for confirmation** — this is a genuine ambiguity in the parameter spec worth resolving explicitly before Stage 3.

---

### 3. Bitcrusher / Sample Rate Reducer
- **JUCE Class:** None — custom implementation
- **Purpose:** Bit-depth quantization and sample-and-hold style sample-rate reduction.
- **Parameters Affected:** `bitDepth`, `sampleRateReduction`
- **Configuration:**
  - Bit reduction: `levels = 2^bitDepth; y = round(x * levels) / levels` per sample
  - Sample-rate reduction: sample-and-hold counter — hold last output sample for `sampleRateReduction` input samples before updating (classic S&H downsampler, no JUCE class exists for this)
  - Both bypass cleanly at `bitDepth=16, sampleRateReduction=1` (defaults = transparent)
  - Should run **inside the Oversampling wrapper** (component #12) since bit/SRR quantization is a strong aliasing source

---

### 4. Glitch / Buffer Engine (18 Modes)
- **JUCE Class:** None — custom `GlitchEngine` built on `juce::AudioBuffer<float>` ring buffer + `juce::dsp::DelayLine<float, juce::dsp::DelayLineInterpolationTypes::Lagrange3rd>` for smooth variable-rate reads
- **Purpose:** Real-time buffer manipulation across 18 modes.
- **Parameters Affected:** `glitchMode`, `glitchBufferLength`, `glitchProbability`, `chaos`
- **Configuration:**
  - Circular buffer sized for the maximum musical division (4 bars at slowest supported tempo, e.g. 4 bars @ 40bpm @ 192kHz — allocate generously in `prepareToPlay`, never on audio thread)
  - `glitchBufferLength` (1/64 to 4 bars) converts to sample count via host BPM (from `juce::AudioPlayHead`)
  - Per-mode implementation notes:
    - **Stutter/Repeat/Retrigger/Micro Loop:** replay a captured window repeatedly (ring buffer read pointer reset to window start each cycle)
    - **Reverse:** decrement read pointer instead of increment
    - **Buffer Repeat/Random Repeat:** capture window, replay N times with optional random window re-selection
    - **Freeze:** hold read pointer static, loop a very short (~single-cycle) window
    - **Slice/Random Slice:** subdivide captured window into slices, play in order or shuffled (`juce::Random`)
    - **Granular Repeat:** short overlapping grains with windowing (Hann window via `juce::dsp::WindowingFunction`) — this is the most CPU/complexity-intensive mode
    - **Tape Stop/Tape Start:** ramp playback rate from 1.0→0.0 (stop) or 0.0→1.0 (start) over a musically-timed ramp, read via `DelayLine` fractional-index interpolated read
    - **Pitch Jump:** instant playback-rate multiplier change (musical intervals) using the same fractional-rate read mechanism as tape stop/start
    - **Silence:** hard/soft-gated mute for the window duration
    - **Noise Burst/Bitcrush Burst:** inject `juce::Random`-generated noise, or route buffer through component #3 at an extreme fixed setting, for the trigger duration
  - `glitchProbability` gates whether each rhythmic trigger event actually fires (Bernoulli trial per event using `juce::Random`)
  - `chaos` (global) scales probability variance and adds controlled random jitter to buffer window selection/length; **must use a seeded `juce::Random` instance (not the shared global RNG) so presets reproduce identical glitch behavior across sessions** — seed stored in custom state (see State Persistence)

---

### 5. Rhythmic Sequencer
- **JUCE Class:** `juce::AudioPlayHead` (host tempo/PPQ query via `getPosition()` → `std::optional<juce::AudioPlayHead::PositionInfo>`, JUCE 8 API) — everything else is a custom `StepSequencer` class
- **Purpose:** Host-synced 16/32-step sequencer modulating up to 10 destination lanes.
- **Parameters Affected:** `sequencerSteps`, `sequencerRate` (automatable); per-step pattern data (custom, non-APVTS state — see below)
- **Configuration:**
  - Step advance computed from host PPQ position and `sequencerRate` (1/4 through 1/16T note divisions)
  - **MVP is host-synced only** — if `getPosition()` returns `std::nullopt` or `isPlaying() == false` (e.g. Standalone with no transport, or host doesn't provide position), sequencer must freeze at step 0 / hold last value rather than crash or silently free-run (explicit fallback behavior required, not specified in brief — flagged as an implementation decision)
  - Per-step values for each of 10 lanes (Drive, Mix, Filter Cutoff, Bit Depth, Sample Rate, Glitch Probability, Volume, Pan, Pitch, Gate) are stored as **custom `juce::ValueTree` state, NOT individual APVTS parameters** — at 32 steps × 10 lanes = 320 values, making these APVTS parameters would explode the automatable parameter count and is not how comparable products (Stepic, Effectrix) expose step data (steps are pattern data, not per-step host-automatable parameters). Pattern operations (Random, Mutate, Reverse, Mirror, Shift, Half, Double, Syncopate, Clear, Humanize) mutate this ValueTree on the message thread; audio thread reads a lock-free double-buffered snapshot (pointer swap, same pattern as DrumRoulette's sample-buffer swap)
  - Sequencer output values feed into the same modulation-summing mechanism as the Mod Matrix (see component #8) — i.e., "Sequencer" is one of the Mod Matrix's available sources, and the 10 fixed lanes are effectively a pre-wired sequencer→destination mapping layered underneath the free-form matrix

---

### 6. Filter Stage
- **JUCE Class:** `juce::dsp::StateVariableTPTFilter<float>` (LP/HP/BP/Resonant LP/Resonant HP) + `juce::dsp::IIR::Filter<float>` with `juce::dsp::IIR::Coefficients<float>::makeNotch()` (Notch) + custom comb filter built from `juce::dsp::DelayLine<float>` with feedback gain (Comb)
- **Purpose:** Selectable filter topology, positioned post-Glitch per the reconciled MVP chain.
- **Parameters Affected:** `filterType`, `filterCutoff`, `filterResonance`
- **Configuration:**
  - `filterCutoff` 20Hz-20kHz, logarithmic skew
  - `filterResonance` 0-100% → StateVariableTPTFilter's `resonance`/Q parameter (clamped to prevent self-oscillation blowup at extreme settings, esp. relevant since Filter also sits inside the Feedback Routing loop — see component #7)
  - `StateVariableTPTFilter::Type` does not include a native Notch mode in JUCE 8 — Notch requires the separate `IIR::Filter` path (coefficient recalculation on `filterCutoff`/`filterResonance` change, done on audio thread without allocation per `juce8-critical-patterns.md` guidance for `juce::dsp` components)
  - Comb: short delay line (~1-20ms, tunable via `filterCutoff` reinterpreted as comb spacing when `filterType=Comb`) with feedback coefficient derived from `filterResonance`
  - Filter must reset state (`.reset()`) on `filterType` change to prevent transient bursts (documented pattern from GainKnob reference plugin)

---

### 7. Feedback Routing Path (DISTORTION → FILTER → DELAY → DISTORTION)
- **JUCE Class:** Reuses components #2 (Distortion) and #6 (Filter) + `juce::dsp::DelayLine<float>` (short feedback delay) + custom safety-limiter/soft-clamp
- **Purpose:** Controlled internal feedback loop for self-generating textures, confirmed IN for MVP with conservative auto-limiting.
- **Parameters Affected:** `feedbackAmount`, `feedbackDamping`
- **Configuration:**
  - Signal tapped post-Distortion, routed through a copy of the Filter stage's current settings, through a short `DelayLine` (recommend 1-50ms, tunable or fixed — brief doesn't specify a feedback-loop delay time parameter, only Feedback/Damping/Filter controls, so **delay time is likely a fixed or minimal-range internal constant for MVP**, flagged as a spec gap to confirm), then summed back into the Distortion stage's input for the next block
  - **Safety design (non-negotiable per brief):**
    1. `feedbackAmount` (0-100% UI range) is mapped through a **non-linear soft-clamp curve** (e.g. `internalGain = 0.9 * tanh(feedbackAmount)` or similar saturating map) so the *parameter itself* can never command unity/runaway gain, regardless of setting
    2. `feedbackDamping` drives a one-pole lowpass (`juce::dsp::IIR::Filter::makeLowPass` or `juce::dsp::FirstOrderTPTFilter`) inside the loop — HF energy is attenuated every pass, which is what prevents feedback from building into harsh runaway noise over many iterations even before the gain clamp
    3. **Per-block finite check:** after computing the feedback sample, verify `std::isfinite()`; if a NaN/Inf is ever detected, hard-reset the feedback delay line and any filter state to zero for that channel (a "circuit breaker" — cheap, real-time-safe, and audio-thread-legal since it's just a buffer clear, no allocation)
    4. Consider an additional block-level RMS-based limiter on the feedback path specifically (separate from the main Output Limiter, component #13) so the loop's own recirculating energy is bounded even before it reaches the master output stage
  - This is one of the highest-risk components in the whole plugin (see Implementation Risks below) — get this right before building anything downstream of it, since instability here corrupts everything after

---

### 8. Modulation Matrix + 4 LFOs
- **JUCE Class:** No single JUCE class covers this — custom `Lfo` class (phase accumulator, all 9 shapes) × 4 instances, custom `ModMatrix` class, `juce::dsp::BallisticsFilter<float>` (Envelope source / Audio Level source), `juce::Random` (Random source), `juce::MidiBuffer`/`juce::MidiMessage` (MIDI CC source)
- **Purpose:** Free-routing modulation from 8 sources to a wide destination list, per-slot Amount/Polarity/optional Curve.
- **Parameters Affected:** `lfo1Rate`-`lfo4Rate` (+ shape/sync toggle per LFO — not yet in draft spec, needed for full implementation), Mod Matrix slot parameters (source/destination/amount/polarity per slot — not yet in draft spec)
- **Configuration:**
  - LFO shapes: sine, triangle, saw, reverse saw, square, sample & hold, random, smooth random, random-walk. Only sine/triangle/saw map cleanly onto `juce::dsp::Oscillator`'s waveform-lambda pattern; S&H/random/smooth-random/random-walk require fully custom per-sample logic (S&H = hold `juce::Random` value until phase wraps; smooth-random = S&H target with `SmoothedValue` ramp between targets; random-walk = accumulate small random deltas each phase-wrap, clamped to range) — recommend implementing ALL 9 shapes in one custom `Lfo` class rather than mixing `juce::dsp::Oscillator` + custom, for consistency
  - Free Hz (0.01-20Hz) or tempo-sync (note divisions, using the same `AudioPlayHead` PPQ mechanism as the Sequencer)
  - **Mod Matrix** recommended as a small **fixed number of assignable slots** (e.g. 8 slots, matching the brief's description of "each assignment: Amount, Polarity, optional Curve") rather than a full N×M dense matrix — dense would be 8 sources × ~12 destinations × 3 fields = untenable for both UI and parameter count. Each slot: `sourceChoice` (LFO1-4/Envelope/AudioLevel/Sequencer/Random/MIDICC/Macro), `destinationChoice` (Drive/Mix/Filter/BitDepth/SampleRate/Fold/Feedback/GlitchProbability/GlitchSize/Pan/Width/etc.), `amount` (-100..+100%), optional `curve` (linear/exponential/S-curve)
  - **Recommend implementing slots as APVTS parameters** (choice + choice + float + float per slot × 8 slots) rather than custom ValueTree state — unlike the Sequencer's per-step data (320 values, clearly not automatable), 8 slots × ~4 fields = 32 parameters is within normal APVTS territory and gives hosts automation access to mod routing, matching how comparable hardware/software mod matrices expose routing as recallable state
  - Per-block: for each active slot, read source value (0.0-1.0 or -1.0-1.0 depending on source), apply polarity/curve, scale by amount, sum into a per-destination accumulator; destinations then combine this modulation with their own base APVTS value + Macro contribution (component #9) + Sequencer lane contribution (component #5) — **all three modulation layers (Sequencer lanes, Mod Matrix, Macros) write into the same per-parameter accumulator once per block**, this unification is the most important integration point in the whole architecture (see Integration Points below)

---

### 9. Macro System (8 Macros)
- **JUCE Class:** APVTS float parameters (8×) + `juce::SmoothedValue<float>` per affected destination
- **Purpose:** Each macro drives a fixed, hand-tuned combination of underlying parameters simultaneously.
- **Parameters Affected:** `macroDamage`, `macroCrush`, `macroGlitch`, `macroChaos`, `macroRhythm`, `macroMovement`, `macroWidth`, `macroMix`
- **Configuration:**
  - Custom `MacroEngine`: fixed internal routing table (code-defined, NOT user-editable for MVP — brief doesn't request macro-destination customization) mapping each macro to a list of `{targetParamID, weight, curve}` tuples, e.g.:
    - `macroDamage` → Drive (+weight), Fold-bias-toward-clip (+weight), Feedback Amount (+weight)
    - `macroCrush` → Bit Depth (-weight, i.e. reduces depth as macro increases), Sample Rate Reduction (+weight)
    - `macroGlitch` → Glitch Probability (+weight), Buffer repeat intensity (+weight), Sample Rate Reduction (+weight, shared with Crush), Pitch variation (+weight)
    - `macroChaos` → global `chaos` param scaling + Mod Matrix "Random" source depth
    - `macroRhythm` → Sequencer/Glitch gate intensity, `glitchProbability`
    - `macroMovement` → LFO depth multiplier across all 4 LFOs' Mod Matrix contributions
    - `macroWidth` → stereo width param (deferred to post-MVP Stereo module — for MVP, this macro has a reduced/no-op effect until Stereo ships, flagged as a scope gap)
    - `macroMix` → mirrors master `mix`, supports >100%
  - Macros combine additively with Mod Matrix + Sequencer contributions per destination (same unified accumulator described in component #8)

---

### 10. XY Pad (with Inertia)
- **JUCE Class:** `juce::SmoothedValue<float>` (or `juce::dsp::LinearSmoothedValue<float>`) per axis
- **Purpose:** Performance-instrument-feel 2D control gliding toward touch/drag targets rather than snapping instantly.
- **Parameters Affected:** `xyPadX`, `xyPadY`, `xyPadSmoothing`
- **Configuration:**
  - WebView UI reports raw target position on drag; C++ side calls `SmoothedValue::setTargetValue()` and lets the built-in ramp (`reset(sampleRate, xyPadSmoothing/1000.0)`) glide toward it every block — this is the standard, correct JUCE mechanism for exactly this "glide, not snap" requirement; no custom physics/spring simulation needed
  - Default mapping: X→`macroDamage`, Y→`macroGlitch`, but "either axis can control any macro or parameter" per brief — recommend a small internal routing choice param (`xyPadXTarget`, `xyPadYTarget`, choice type) rather than hardcoding
  - `xyPadSmoothing` (0-500ms) is itself just the ramp time fed to the two `SmoothedValue` instances

---

### 11. Performance Mode Triggers (7)
- **JUCE Class:** `juce::AudioParameterBool` (×7) via `getToggleState()` WebView binding (critical pattern #19)
- **Purpose:** Large, live-performance, MIDI-triggerable buttons for instant dramatic state changes.
- **Parameters Affected:** `performanceKill`, `performanceGlitch`, `performanceDestroy`, `performanceFreeze`, `performanceReverse`, `performanceStutter`, `performanceChaos`
- **Configuration:**
  - Each trigger applies a fixed "preset diff" (code-defined delta/override set on relevant params — e.g. `performanceFreeze` forces `glitchMode=Freeze` + near-zero glitch buffer length while active) via the same unified modulation-accumulator pattern used by Macros/Mod Matrix, applied as a high-priority override layer (trigger overrides win over macro/matrix contributions while active)
  - MIDI-triggerable: no built-in JUCE "MIDI learn" class — custom fixed or user-assignable MIDI CC/Note-to-trigger mapping table, read from `juce::MidiBuffer` each block, calling `setValueNotifyingHost()` on the corresponding `AudioParameterBool`
  - Momentary vs. toggle behavior per trigger — recommend a simple internal flag per trigger (not necessarily user-configurable for MVP; brief doesn't specify per-trigger customization)

---

### 12. Oversampling / Quality Engine
- **JUCE Class:** `juce::dsp::Oversampling<float>`
- **Purpose:** User-selectable oversampling around nonlinear stages to control aliasing.
- **Parameters Affected:** `qualityMode`
- **Configuration:**
  - ECO = 1x (no oversampling), NORMAL = 2x, HIGH = 4x, EXTREME = 8x — straightforward `juce::dsp::Oversampling` factor selection, using FIR polyphase (`filterType = FilterType::filterHalfBandFIREquiripple`) for quality or IIR for lower latency, tradeoff to be decided in Stage 3
  - `AUTO` has no direct JUCE equivalent — custom heuristic needed (e.g. scale oversampling factor with current Drive/Fold intensity, or with detected CPU headroom); **this is the vaguest-specified parameter value in the whole spec and needs a concrete decision rule before Stage 3 implementation** (flagged as risk)
  - Oversampling wraps: Distortion Engine (#2), Bitcrusher/SRR (#3), and the nonlinear elements inside Feedback Routing (#7) — NOT the Glitch Engine (buffer manipulation doesn't alias the same way) or Filter/Sequencer/Mod Matrix (linear/control-rate, no benefit)
  - **CRITICAL:** must call `setLatencySamples()` on the processor to report oversampling-induced latency for host PDC (Plugin Delay Compensation) — easy to forget, high risk of "audio sounds phasey when blended with other tracks" bug if skipped
  - Changing `qualityMode` at runtime requires re-preparing the `Oversampling` object (not safe to resize on the audio thread) — needs a message-thread-triggered `prepare()` call with the new factor, careful not to glitch playback (common pattern: prepare new instance off-thread, atomic pointer swap)

---

### 13. Output Limiter (Dual-Mode)
- **JUCE Class:** `juce::dsp::Limiter<float>` (Transparent mode) + `juce::dsp::WaveShaper<float>` (Colored mode's added saturation)
- **Purpose:** Final safety net, with an optional character mode.
- **Parameters Affected:** `outputLimiterStyle`, `outputGain`
- **Configuration:**
  - Transparent: `juce::dsp::Limiter` alone — a pure peak-catcher, minimal coloration
  - Colored: brief describes "adds gentle saturation/character on limiting" — `juce::dsp::Limiter` does not expose a gain-reduction signal to key off of, so the technically-correct "saturate proportional to GR" behavior is NOT directly available from the stock class
    - **Recommended MVP approach (Risk: MEDIUM):** apply a fixed, gentle waveshaper saturation stage always-on in Colored mode, positioned just before the limiter (so it colors material that's already near the ceiling more than quiet material, an approximation of "colors when limiting"), rather than building a custom GR-aware limiter for MVP
    - **Fallback/future approach:** implement a custom limiter (peak detector + gain-smoother, akin to `juce::dsp::Compressor` internals with near-infinite ratio + lookahead) to get true GR-proportional coloring — HIGHER complexity, deferred unless the fixed-saturation approximation sounds unconvincing in testing
  - `outputGain` (-24..+24dB) applied after the limiter (standard trim, not limited)

---

### 14. Master Mix Stage
- **JUCE Class:** Custom (NOT `juce::dsp::DryWetMixer`, see rationale) — two `juce::SmoothedValue<float>` gain coefficients (dry, wet)
- **Purpose:** Dry/wet blend supporting the brief's non-standard 0-200% range (>100% lets wet dominate/overdrive the blend).
- **Parameters Affected:** `mix`
- **Configuration:**
  - 0-100%: standard equal-power or linear crossfade (`dryGain = 1-mix, wetGain = mix`)
  - 100-200%: dry continues toward 0 (or stays at 0, TBD in Stage 3) while wet gain ramps above 1.0 up to a ceiling (e.g. +6dB at 200%) for the "parallel-style boost" effect described in the brief
  - `juce::dsp::DryWetMixer` is built around a 0-100% (0.0-1.0) proportion model with latency-compensated crossfading — it doesn't natively support the >100% overdrive behavior, so a custom two-gain implementation is simpler than fighting the built-in class's API for this one non-standard requirement
  - This must be the LAST stage before Output Limiter, capturing dry signal at the very start of `processBlock()` (before Input Gain, to match user expectation that "dry" means the original unprocessed signal, not post-input-gain)

## Processing Chain

```
INPUT
  ↓ (dry signal captured here for Master Mix, component #14)
Input Gain ← inputGain
  ↓
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Oversampling Engine UP-SAMPLE ← qualityMode │
│  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐│
│  │ Distortion Engine ← distortionAlgorithm, ││
│  │   drive, tone, bias, fold, distortionMix ││
│  │   ↓                                      ││
│  │ Bitcrusher / SRR ← bitDepth,             ││
│  │   sampleRateReduction                    ││
│  └─────────────────────────────────────────┘│
│  Oversampling Engine DOWN-SAMPLE             │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────┘
  ↓
Glitch / Buffer Engine ← glitchMode, glitchBufferLength,
  glitchProbability, chaos
  ↓
Filter Stage ← filterType, filterCutoff, filterResonance
  ↓
  ├──(tap)──→ Feedback Routing Path ──→ (sum back into
  │            [Filter copy → short Delay → safety     Distortion Engine
  │             soft-clamp/limiter, NaN guard]          input, next block)
  │            ← feedbackAmount, feedbackDamping
  ↓
Master Mix ← mix (dry captured pre-Input-Gain; wet = signal here)
  ↓
Output Gain ← outputGain
  ↓
Output Limiter ← outputLimiterStyle
  ↓
OUTPUT

[Parallel/side systems feeding parameters at every block, not part of the
 linear signal path above:]

  Rhythmic Sequencer (host-synced) ──┐
  4× LFO (free/tempo-synced) ────────┤
  Envelope Follower / Audio Level ───┼──→ Mod Matrix (8 slots) ──┐
  Random source ──────────────────────┤                          │
  MIDI CC ────────────────────────────┘                          │
                                                                  ├──→ Unified per-parameter
  8× Macro controls ──────────────────────────────────────────────┤   modulation accumulator
                                                                  │   (base APVTS value +
  XY Pad (2 axes, smoothed) ──→ drives assigned Macro(s) ─────────┤    Sequencer lane +
                                                                  │    Mod Matrix + Macro +
  7× Performance Mode triggers (MIDI-triggerable, highest ────────┘    Performance override)
    priority override) ────────────────────────────────────────────→ applied to every
                                                                        modulatable param
                                                                        above, once per block
```

**Routing notes:**
- The Feedback Routing Path is the one deliberate loop in an otherwise linear chain — everything else is strictly sequential.
- Sequencer, Mod Matrix, Macros, and Performance Triggers do NOT sit "in" the linear signal path; they are a parallel control-rate system that writes modulated values into the same parameters the linear chain reads every block. This is why the "Unified per-parameter modulation accumulator" is the single most important integration point (see Integration Points).
- Oversampling brackets only the Distortion + Bitcrush/SRR stages (and, separately, the nonlinear element inside the Feedback loop) — Glitch, Filter, Mix, and Limiter run at the plugin's native sample rate.

---

## System Architecture

### MIDI Routing

**Input handling:** Omni mode. CORRUPTR is an audio effect (not an instrument) — MIDI input is used exclusively for control (Performance Mode trigger mapping, optional XY Pad MIDI control, Mod Matrix "MIDI CC" source), never for note-triggered synthesis.

**Note/CC mapping:**
- Performance Mode triggers: fixed or user-assignable MIDI CC/Note → `AudioParameterBool::setValueNotifyingHost()` (custom mapping table, no built-in JUCE MIDI-learn)
- Mod Matrix "MIDI CC" source: any incoming CC value (0-127 → 0.0-1.0) usable as a modulation source in an assigned slot
- XY Pad: optional MIDI CC control of X/Y position (brief: "Optional MIDI control") — same CC-to-target mechanism as above

**JUCE classes:**
- `juce::MidiBuffer` — iterate incoming MIDI in `processBlock()`
- `juce::MidiMessage::isController()`, `getControllerNumber()`, `getControllerValue()` — CC extraction
- `juce::MidiMessage::isNoteOn()` — for Note-triggered Performance Mode buttons if supported

**Processing:** MIDI parsed once per block on the audio thread; no background thread needed (no file I/O, no MIDI file parsing).

**Thread safety:** All MIDI handling stays on the audio thread; UI-driven MIDI-mapping changes (if user-assignable is implemented) communicate via atomics, same pattern as other cross-thread parameter communication.

---

### State Persistence

**What state is saved:**
- APVTS parameters: ~85-90 automatable float/choice/bool parameters (automatic via `AudioProcessorValueTreeState`)
- Custom (non-APVTS) state:
  - Sequencer pattern data: up to 32 steps × 10 lanes of per-step values (`juce::ValueTree`)
  - Glitch Engine's deterministic random seed (for reproducible chaos/randomization across sessions — brief explicitly requires this)
  - Randomization mode seeds for SAFE/CREATIVE/EXTREME random (if seeded, not fully non-deterministic)
  - Performance Mode MIDI mapping table, if user-assignable (else fixed in code, no persistence needed)

**Serialization format:**
- APVTS: automatic XML via `ValueTree::toXmlString()`
- Custom state: nested `juce::ValueTree` merged into the same state blob returned from `getStateInformation()`, following the DrumRoulette pattern (APVTS ValueTree + custom child ValueTree combined into one XML document)

**JUCE classes:**
- `juce::AudioProcessorValueTreeState` — parameter persistence
- `juce::ValueTree` — sequencer pattern + seed state
- `juce::XmlElement` — combined serialization

**Restore behavior:**
- Missing/corrupt custom state: fall back to a default empty pattern (all steps at "no modulation") and a fresh random seed — never crash on malformed preset data
- Version migration: not needed for MVP (no prior version exists), but recommend a `version` attribute in the root ValueTree from day one to ease future migrations (cheap insurance, standard practice)

## Algorithm Details

### Distortion Engine — Wavefolder/Foldback Transfer Function
**Algorithm:** Triangle-wave folding — reflect the signal back into range every time it crosses ±threshold, iterated `fold` times.
**Implementation notes:**
- `y = triangleFold(x * (1 + fold*k))` where `triangleFold` maps any input onto a repeating triangle ramp between -1 and 1 (`asin(sin(x*pi/2))`-style closed form, or an iterative reflect loop)
- Foldback differs from Wavefolder by threshold/reflection curve shape (softer knee) rather than a different core algorithm — implement as a shared function with a shape parameter
- No oversampling-free option — this generates strong high-frequency content and MUST run inside the Oversampling wrapper

### Bitcrusher / SRR — Combined Quantize + Hold
**Algorithm:** `y[n] = quantize(hold(x[n], srrFactor), bitDepth)`
**Implementation notes:**
- Hold state is per-channel (2 counters + 2 held-sample floats for stereo)
- Quantization: `round(x * (2^bitDepth - 1)) / (2^bitDepth - 1)`, careful with `bitDepth=1` edge case (must not divide by zero — `2^1-1=1` is fine, but validate the full 1-16 range doesn't hit a degenerate case)

### Feedback Safety Soft-Clamp
**Algorithm:** `internalFeedbackGain = maxSafeGain * tanh(feedbackAmount / 100.0)`, where `maxSafeGain` is a code constant well below 1.0 (e.g. 0.85) chosen so that even with maximum damping-off and worst-case loop delay/filter combination, the loop is mathematically guaranteed to converge (geometric series with ratio < 1)
**Implementation notes:**
- This must be validated with an actual worst-case sine-sweep / impulse test during Stage 3 (automated test category "feedback stability" is explicitly called out in the brief's Testing Notes)
- Combine with per-block `std::isfinite()` circuit-breaker as the last line of defense, not the primary safety mechanism (the gain clamp + damping filter should make the breaker never trip in normal use — if it trips often during testing, the clamp constant needs tightening)

---

## Integration Points

### Feature Dependencies

- Distortion Engine → Bitcrusher/SRR: sequential, no shared state (both always process, distortionAlgorithm choice doesn't disable Bitcrusher)
- Glitch Engine → everything downstream: Glitch reorders/repeats time, so Filter/Feedback/Mix all process whatever the Glitch Engine currently outputs, including its non-linear time behavior (tape stop/reverse) — Filter and Feedback Routing must be robust to sudden discontinuities in the signal from Glitch mode switches
- Feedback Routing → Distortion Engine: feedback output sums into next block's Distortion input, creating the loop; Distortion Engine's oversampling wrapper therefore also processes recirculated feedback energy, which affects the safety-clamp math (component must be validated with feedback active, not just dry-signal Distortion)
- Sequencer/Mod Matrix/Macros/Performance Triggers → ALL modulatable parameters: this is the single largest integration surface in the plugin — every parameter listed in the Parameter Mapping table above that isn't purely structural (choice-of-topology types like `filterType`, `distortionAlgorithm`, `glitchMode`, `qualityMode` are typically NOT continuously modulated, only their continuous siblings like cutoff/drive/etc. are) needs to accept a per-block modulation offset from up to four simultaneous sources (base value, Sequencer lane, Mod Matrix slot(s), Macro contribution) plus a possible Performance Trigger override
- Oversampling → Distortion Engine + Bitcrusher/SRR + Feedback nonlinear element: these three MUST be processed inside the same oversampled block for the aliasing control to be coherent; splitting them across separate oversampling contexts would be wasteful and could introduce phase mismatches between the feedback-forward and feedback-return paths

### Parameter Interactions

- `feedbackAmount` + `filterResonance` (when Filter sits inside the loop): high resonance inside a high-feedback loop is the single most dangerous parameter combination in the plugin — resonance can itself add gain at the cutoff frequency, compounding with the feedback loop's own gain. The safety soft-clamp (component #7) must be validated against this specific combination, not just against `feedbackAmount` in isolation.
- `mix` (master, 0-200%) vs. `distortionMix` (stage-local, 0-100%): these are independent and can compound — a user driving both to their maximum gets full-wet distortion AND up to +6dB "overdrive" on top from the master mix >100% behavior. Not a bug, but worth an explicit implementation note so it isn't "fixed" as an unintended interaction later.
- `qualityMode=AUTO` interacts with `drive`/`fold` (whatever heuristic is chosen) and therefore indirectly with CPU load — this is the one parameter whose behavior depends on OTHER parameters' values by design, unlike everything else in the spec which is independently addressable.
- Macro contributions and Mod Matrix contributions can target the same destination simultaneously (e.g. `macroDamage` and a Mod Matrix slot both modulating `drive`) — both must combine additively without one silently overriding the other, and the combined result must still be clamped to the parameter's valid range before being applied (a modulated `drive` value must never exceed 40dB or go negative in a way the waveshaper can't handle).

### Processing Order Requirements

**Sequential DSP chain (per block, REQUIRED order):**
1. Capture dry signal (before Input Gain) — for Master Mix
2. Apply unified modulation accumulator to all modulatable parameters for this block (Sequencer + Mod Matrix + Macros + Performance Trigger overrides, all combined) — must happen BEFORE any DSP component reads its "current" parameter value, since every component below reads modulated values, not raw APVTS values
3. Input Gain
4. Oversampling up-sample
5. Distortion Engine (using this block's feedback-loop-recirculated sample as part of its input, from step 10 of the PREVIOUS block)
6. Bitcrusher/SRR
7. Oversampling down-sample
8. Glitch Engine
9. Filter Stage
10. Feedback Routing tap: copy signal here, run through Filter-copy → Delay → safety clamp → store for step 5 of NEXT block
11. Master Mix (dry from step 1, wet from step 9's output continuing forward)
12. Output Gain
13. Output Limiter

**Why order matters:**
- Modulation must resolve before any DSP reads parameters (step 2 before 3) — otherwise different components in the same block could read inconsistent parameter snapshots if modulation were applied lazily/per-component
- Feedback tap (step 10) happens post-Filter, pre-Mix — matches the brief's explicit `DISTORTION → FILTER → DELAY → DISTORTION` loop description, and ensures the feedback loop doesn't include the Master Mix's dry signal (which would corrupt the dry/wet blend concept)
- Oversampling only brackets steps 5-6, not the whole chain — Glitch/Filter/Mix run at native rate

**Parallel processing notes:** None of the core chain can run in parallel (strictly sequential signal path). The Sequencer/LFOs/Mod Matrix computation (step 2's inputs) CAN be computed independently of each other before summing, but that's an internal optimization detail, not an architectural requirement.

### Thread Boundaries

**Audio thread:**
- Entire linear DSP chain (Input Gain → ... → Output Limiter)
- Modulation accumulator computation (Sequencer/LFO/Mod Matrix/Macro/Trigger summing) — all real-time-safe, no allocation, reads pre-computed pattern data via lock-free snapshot
- MIDI parsing (Performance Trigger mapping, Mod Matrix MIDI CC source)
- Feedback loop state and NaN circuit-breaker

**Message thread:**
- All APVTS parameter writes (from WebView UI interaction)
- Sequencer pattern editing (Random/Mutate/Reverse/Mirror/Shift/etc. pattern operations) — writes to a "staging" `ValueTree`, then atomically swaps a pointer/snapshot the audio thread reads, same double-buffer pattern as DrumRoulette's sample buffers
- XY Pad drag target updates (feeds `SmoothedValue::setTargetValue()`, which itself is read on the audio thread every block — this specific call is safe from either thread per JUCE's `SmoothedValue` design, but the *source* of the target — WebView drag events — arrives on the message thread)
- Preset load/save, Randomization trigger button

**No background thread needed:** MVP has no file I/O (no sample loading, no folder scanning) — unlike DrumRoulette, CORRUPTR's state is entirely synthesized/parametric.

**Communication mechanisms:**
- APVTS: atomic reads (audio thread) / atomic writes (message thread), standard JUCE mechanism
- Sequencer pattern: double-buffered `ValueTree` snapshot, pointer swap (lock-free)
- Glitch/Randomization seeds: `std::atomic<uint32_t>` or similar, read once per relevant trigger event, not per-sample
- Oversampling factor changes (`qualityMode`): message-thread-triggered re-`prepare()` on a new `Oversampling` instance, atomic pointer swap into the audio thread's active instance (never resize/reallocate the currently-in-use instance from the audio thread)

---

## Implementation Risks

### Feedback Routing Path (Safety-Critical)
**Complexity:** HIGH
**Risk Level:** HIGH
**Risk factors:**
1. Runaway feedback is a real risk to users' ears/speakers if the soft-clamp math is wrong — this is the one component where a bug isn't just "sounds bad," it's potentially harmful
2. Interacts dangerously with `filterResonance` (see Parameter Interactions above)
3. NaN/Inf propagation through a feedback loop can persist indefinitely (a single bad sample recirculates forever without an explicit reset) unlike a purely feedforward chain where a bad sample eventually flushes through
4. No JUCE class handles any part of this — fully custom, high scrutiny required

**Alternative approaches:**
1. **Hard-limit the loop with a `juce::dsp::Limiter` inside the loop itself** (not just a soft-clamp on the gain parameter) — more CPU, but provides a hard mathematical ceiling independent of the tanh-based gain mapping. Recommended as a belt-and-suspenders addition, not a replacement.
2. **Disable feedback entirely as a fallback** (`feedbackAmount` forced to 0, loop bypassed) if testing reveals the safety mechanism is unreliable — last resort, would break a brief-confirmed MVP feature, only acceptable if no safe implementation is achievable in the available time.

**Fallback architecture:**
- Primary: soft-clamp gain mapping (tanh) + in-loop damping filter + per-block finite-check circuit breaker
- Fallback 1: add an in-loop `juce::dsp::Limiter` as a hard ceiling on top of the primary approach
- Fallback 2 (last resort): reduce `feedbackAmount` max range further (e.g. cap UI at what maps to 50% of `maxSafeGain` instead of 100%) if testing shows instability even at nominal "max" settings

**Mitigation strategy:**
1. Implement and unit-test the feedback loop in isolation (synthetic sine/impulse input) before integrating with the rest of the chain
2. Automated test explicitly for feedback stability is already called out in the brief's Testing Notes — treat this as non-optional, not a nice-to-have
3. Sweep `feedbackAmount` × `feedbackDamping` × `filterResonance` combinations in automated tests, checking output RMS never grows unbounded over a sustained test signal

---

### Glitch/Buffer Engine (18 Modes)
**Complexity:** HIGH
**Risk Level:** MEDIUM-HIGH
**Risk factors:**
1. 18 distinct modes is a large surface area — several (Granular Repeat, Tape Stop/Start, Pitch Jump) require variable-rate fractional-index buffer reads with interpolation, meaningfully harder than simple fixed-rate stutter/repeat
2. Buffer sizing must accommodate the slowest supported tempo × longest division (4 bars) — memory and edge-case correctness (extremely long buffers at very low host BPM) need explicit handling
3. Mode-switching mid-playback (e.g. user changes `glitchMode` while a glitch event is actively playing) can produce clicks/discontinuities if not cross-faded or reset cleanly

**Alternative approaches:**
1. **Tiered MVP-within-MVP:** implement the 6-8 simplest modes first (Stutter, Repeat, Reverse, Freeze, Silence, Retrigger) as a functional core, then layer in the more complex modes (Granular Repeat, Tape Stop/Start, Pitch Jump, Slice/Random Slice) — this is explicitly reflected in the phase breakdown in `plan.md`
2. If Granular Repeat proves too CPU/complexity-costly for the available time, it can degrade gracefully to a simpler "short buffer repeat" mode as a reduced-scope fallback (same UI slot, simpler DSP underneath)

**Fallback architecture:**
- Primary: full custom `GlitchEngine` with all 18 modes
- Fallback: ship with the 6-8 simplest modes fully polished for v1.0, remaining modes as a fast-follow update — better than shipping all 18 half-working

**Mitigation strategy:**
- Build and test each mode incrementally with dedicated unit tests (silence in, known pattern in, verify expected buffer manipulation)
- Cross-fade (short linear ramp, ~2-5ms) on every mode transition and every buffer-window reset to eliminate clicks

---

### Rhythmic Sequencer (Host Sync Only)
**Complexity:** MEDIUM
**Risk Level:** MEDIUM
**Risk factors:**
1. MVP explicitly has NO free-run internal clock — behavior when the host provides no transport (Standalone with no play, or hosts with incomplete `AudioPlayHead` support) is unspecified in the brief and needs an explicit fallback decision (documented above: freeze at step 0)
2. 10 modulation lanes × up to 32 steps is meaningful pattern-data complexity, plus 10 pattern-operations (Random/Mutate/Reverse/Mirror/Shift/Half/Double/Syncopate/Clear/Humanize) each need correct, tested implementations
3. `juce::AudioPlayHead::getPosition()` API changed across JUCE versions — JUCE 8 uses `std::optional<PositionInfo>` return; older tutorials/examples show the deprecated `getCurrentPosition(CurrentPositionInfo&)` pattern, a likely source of implementation errors if outdated references are consulted

**Alternative approaches:**
1. Pattern operations could be implemented as a smaller "must-have" set for v1.0 (Random, Reverse, Clear, Shift) with the rest (Mutate, Mirror, Half, Double, Syncopate, Humanize) as fast-follow if time is constrained

**Fallback architecture:**
- Primary: all 10 lanes, all 10 pattern operations, full 16/32-step support
- Fallback: reduce to fewer lanes (e.g. Drive/Mix/Filter/Volume only) if the full 10-lane implementation proves too time-costly, expand later

**Mitigation strategy:**
- Confirm `AudioPlayHead::getPosition()` usage against current JUCE 8 API (not older tutorials) at Stage 3 implementation time
- Explicit "no transport" test case in automated tests (brief's Testing Notes calls out automation/preset-restore testing broadly; extend to include no-transport sequencer behavior)

---

### Unified Modulation Accumulator (Sequencer + Mod Matrix + Macros + Performance Triggers)
**Complexity:** MEDIUM-HIGH
**Risk Level:** MEDIUM
**Risk factors:**
1. This isn't a single "feature" but an architectural pattern threading through nearly every other component — getting the summing/priority/clamping logic wrong subtly affects everything downstream, and bugs here are hard to isolate (could look like "the Distortion Engine is broken" when the real bug is in how modulation combines before Distortion ever reads its `drive` value)
2. Four simultaneous contributors (base + Sequencer + Mod Matrix + Macro) plus Performance Trigger overrides need a well-defined combination order (additive vs. override) per destination

**Alternative approaches:**
1. Simplify for MVP: Performance Triggers are hard overrides (win outright while active); Sequencer/Mod Matrix/Macro combine additively; final result clamped to the parameter's valid range. This is the recommended default — document as the concrete rule.

**Fallback architecture:** N/A — this pattern must exist in some form for the plugin's core identity ("five pillars working together") to function; the fallback is scope-only (fewer simultaneous sources targeting the same destination in early phases, e.g. get Sequencer→Drive working before also layering Mod-Matrix→Drive).

**Mitigation strategy:**
- Build this as its own isolated, unit-tested subsystem BEFORE wiring it into the full DSP chain (validate the accumulator's math with synthetic inputs, independent of actual audio processing)
- Recommended build order: get one destination (e.g. `drive`) working end-to-end with all four contributor types before generalizing to all destinations

---

### Oversampling AUTO Mode
**Complexity:** LOW-MEDIUM (mechanically) but UNDERSPECIFIED (conceptually)
**Risk Level:** MEDIUM
**Risk factors:**
1. No JUCE class or brief-provided rule defines what "AUTO" should actually do — needs a concrete decision (CPU-based? Drive-intensity-based? Fixed at 2x with graceful degradation?) before Stage 3
2. Runtime factor changes require careful `Oversampling` re-`prepare()` without audio-thread reallocation (see component #12)

**Alternative approaches:**
1. Simplest defensible AUTO rule: scale oversampling factor with `drive`/`fold` intensity (louder/more extreme distortion settings get more oversampling, since that's when aliasing is most audible) — recommended as the concrete MVP rule absent further creative-brief guidance
2. CPU-load-based AUTO (measure `processBlock()` duration, back off if approaching budget) is more "correct" for a stated 3-5% CPU target but meaningfully more complex to implement safely — defer unless the drive-based heuristic proves inadequate

**Fallback architecture:** If AUTO proves too ambiguous/risky to implement well in the available time, ship `qualityMode` with ECO/NORMAL/HIGH/EXTREME only for v1.0, add AUTO as a fast-follow once real-world usage data suggests a good heuristic.

**Mitigation strategy:** Get an explicit product decision on the AUTO rule before Stage 3 DSP implementation begins (this is a spec gap, not a DSP-difficulty problem).

---

### Colored Output Limiter
**Complexity:** MEDIUM
**Risk Level:** LOW-MEDIUM
**Risk factors:**
1. `juce::dsp::Limiter` doesn't expose gain-reduction, so "true" GR-proportional coloring isn't directly available from the stock class (see component #13)

**Alternative approaches:** Already detailed in component #13 (fixed always-on gentle saturation as MVP approximation vs. custom GR-aware limiter as future enhancement).

**Fallback architecture:** Transparent-only for v1.0 if the Colored approximation doesn't sound convincing in testing; Colored mode as fast-follow.

**Mitigation strategy:** Prototype both modes early and A/B against reference plugins (SSL X-Limit's "Glue"/"Punch" characters, mentioned in professional research below) before committing to the approximation.

---

### Overall Project Risk

**Overall complexity:** VERY HIGH — see `plan.md` for the numeric complexity score, which exceeds the standard 5.0 cap by a wide margin even before capping.

**Highest risk component:** Feedback Routing Path — the only component with genuine safety implications (runaway audio) rather than "just" implementation difficulty or scope size. Everything else in this risk list is about getting a big scope built correctly and on time; the Feedback Routing Path is about getting it built *safely*.

**Second-highest risk factor: aggregate scope, not any single component.** No individual feature here is undoable — professional plugins ship distortion engines, glitch engines, sequencers, and mod matrices individually all the time. What's unusual is doing all 14 of these simultaneously as a single MVP. See `plan.md` for the explicit recommendation on splitting this into multiple implementation passes.

**Recommended approach:**
1. Build and safety-validate the Feedback Routing Path in isolation FIRST, before any other component depends on it, even though it's not first in the signal chain — its safety property must be proven before the rest of the plugin is built around it
2. Build the Unified Modulation Accumulator as an isolated, tested subsystem SECOND, before wiring Sequencer/Mod Matrix/Macros into it individually
3. Build the linear DSP chain (Input Gain → Distortion → Bitcrush → Glitch(simple modes only) → Filter → Mix → Limiter) as a working core THIRD
4. Layer in Glitch Engine's advanced modes, Sequencer's full lane/pattern-operation set, Mod Matrix's full 8-slot flexibility, all 8 Macros, XY Pad, and Performance Triggers incrementally AFTER the core is stable
5. Oversampling and Quality modes LAST (can be validated against an already-working chain, rather than complicating early debugging with an extra up/down-sample layer)

See `plan.md` for how this maps onto concrete implementation phases.

---

## Architecture Decisions

### Distortion Engine: Single Selectable Algorithm, Not 12 Parallel Stages
**Decision:** `distortionAlgorithm` selects ONE active waveshaper at a time (matches `parameter-spec-draft.md` exactly), not 12 simultaneous processing stages.
**Rationale:** The brief's Signal Chain diagram groups "DISTORTION" as a single chain position; the 12-algorithm list is explicitly framed as "MVP Distortion Algorithm Set," i.e. the menu of choices for that one position, not 12 parallel modules. Parallel/multiband distortion (running several algorithms simultaneously) is explicitly Post-MVP in the brief.
**Alternatives considered:**
1. Multiband-style parallel chain of all 12 — rejected, explicitly Post-MVP per brief
**Tradeoffs accepted:** None significant — this is the reading that matches both the brief's own Post-MVP section and the parameter spec's literal `Choice` type for `distortionAlgorithm`.

### Sequencer Pattern Data as Custom State, Not APVTS Parameters
**Decision:** Per-step, per-lane sequencer values live in a custom `ValueTree`, not as individual `AudioParameterFloat` instances.
**Rationale:** 16-32 steps × 10 lanes = 160-320 values; making each one an APVTS parameter would be both impractical (host parameter lists become unusable at that size) and inconsistent with how comparable products (Stepic, Effectrix) expose step/pattern data as recallable-but-not-individually-automatable state.
**Alternatives considered:**
1. Full APVTS exposure of every step — rejected for parameter-list bloat and host UX concerns
**Tradeoffs accepted:** Individual sequencer steps are NOT independently host-automatable (can't automate "step 3's Drive value" from the DAW timeline) — acceptable because the brief doesn't request per-step automation, only pattern-level operations (Random/Mutate/etc.) which remain available via UI/MIDI-trigger.

### Mod Matrix Slots as APVTS Parameters, Not Custom State
**Decision:** Unlike Sequencer steps, the 8 Mod Matrix slots (source/destination/amount/polarity per slot, ~32 fields total) ARE implemented as APVTS parameters.
**Rationale:** This is a bounded, small parameter count (unlike the Sequencer's 160-320 values) and matches how hardware/software mod matrices typically expose routing as host-automatable, recallable state — a user reasonably expects to automate "increase LFO1→Filter amount over time," which requires the amount to be a real automatable parameter.
**Alternatives considered:**
1. Custom ValueTree (matching Sequencer's approach) — rejected because the smaller scale doesn't justify losing host automation access
**Tradeoffs accepted:** None significant at this scale (32 params well within normal territory for a plugin this size).

### Master Mix Custom Implementation Instead of `juce::dsp::DryWetMixer`
**Decision:** Build Master Mix manually with two smoothed gain coefficients rather than using `juce::dsp::DryWetMixer`.
**Rationale:** The brief's 0-200% range with >100% "wet dominates/overdrives" behavior isn't representable in `DryWetMixer`'s 0.0-1.0 proportion model without fighting the class's API.
**Alternatives considered:**
1. Clamp `DryWetMixer` to 0-100% and implement the >100% boost as a separate post-mix gain stage — considered viable but adds an extra processing stage for something a from-scratch two-gain implementation handles in one place; rejected for unnecessary complexity
**Tradeoffs accepted:** Lose `DryWetMixer`'s built-in latency-compensation delay line — acceptable because CORRUPTR's chain (absent the Feedback loop, which has its own delay) doesn't introduce meaningful dry/wet path latency mismatch requiring compensation.

## Special Considerations

### Thread Safety
- All parameter reads inside the DSP chain use atomic `getRawParameterValue()->load()` or the modulated-value accumulator's own atomic/lock-free snapshot mechanism, never a raw pointer dereference without atomicity guarantees
- Sequencer pattern edits (message thread) → audio thread: double-buffered `ValueTree` snapshot, pointer swap (no locks in audio thread)
- Oversampling factor changes: prepare off audio-thread, atomic pointer swap into active use

### Performance
- Estimated CPU budget per brief: ~3-5% per instance on a modern CPU at default (likely NORMAL/2x oversampling) settings
- Highest-cost components: Oversampling (scales directly with factor: EXTREME/8x will meaningfully exceed the 3-5% target on its own), Glitch Engine's Granular Repeat mode (windowed overlapping grains), Feedback Routing (runs Distortion+Filter twice per block — once forward, once through the loop copy)
- Recommend profiling each component in isolation during Stage 3 rather than only profiling the full chain, given how many components exist

### Denormal Protection
- `juce::ScopedNoDenormals` at the top of `processBlock()`
- Feedback loop's recirculating low-level signal is a classic denormal risk (decaying signal approaching but never reaching zero) — extra attention warranted here specifically, on top of the standard whole-block protection
- Custom LFO phase accumulators should use phase-wrapping (not decaying amplitude) to avoid their own denormal risk

### Sample Rate Handling
- All time-based components (Glitch buffer, Sequencer, LFO rates, Feedback delay, Filter/Comb delay) must recompute sample-count-based internals in `prepareToPlay()` on sample-rate change
- Glitch Engine's ring buffer must be sized for the worst-case sample rate the plugin supports (brief's Testing Notes explicitly list 44.1/48/88.2/96/192kHz) — size for 192kHz, not 48kHz, to avoid reallocation mid-session on rate changes
- Oversampling's internal FIR/IIR filter design is sample-rate-dependent — `juce::dsp::Oversampling::reset()`/re-`prepare()` required on rate change, same as on `qualityMode` change

### Latency
- Oversampling introduces latency proportional to factor (higher at HIGH/EXTREME) — MUST be reported via `setLatencySamples()` for host PDC
- Feedback loop's internal delay does NOT count as reportable plugin latency (it's an internal feedback path, not a forward-path delay) — do not double-report
- Glitch Engine buffer capture does not inherently add latency (it's a ring buffer read/write, not a forward delay) unless a specific mode's implementation requires look-ahead (none currently specified do)

## Research References

### Professional Plugins
1. **iZotope Trash 2** — 60+ distortion algorithms across multiple modules; explicit named inspiration in the brief. Confirms the "single active distortion voice selected from a large menu, with separate always-on utility stages (filter, etc.)" pattern used in this architecture rather than all-simultaneous processing.
2. **Soundtoys Decapitator** — warm-to-aggressive analog-flavored saturation; explicit named inspiration. Its 5-mode "Punish/A/E/N/T" character selector is a smaller-scale precedent for CORRUPTR's `distortionAlgorithm` choice-based approach.
3. **Sugar Bytes Effectrix** — 32-step "matrix" triggering glitch/stutter effects, tempo-synced; closest direct precedent for the Glitch Engine + Sequencer combination CORRUPTR is attempting.
4. **Glitchmachines Fracture** — dedicated buffer/delay/granular engine with adjustable buffer size, repeat count, ratio — directly informs the Glitch Engine's `glitchBufferLength` + mode design.
5. **Output Movement** — combines LFO, step sequencer, sidechain, and an XY pad controlling up to 152 destinations simultaneously; strong precedent for CORRUPTR's unified modulation-accumulator design connecting many sources to many destinations through macro/XY abstraction layers.
6. **SSL X-Limit** — "Transparent/Glue/Punch/Auto" limiter character selector; direct precedent for `outputLimiterStyle`'s Transparent/Colored concept.

### JUCE Documentation (based on JUCE 8 API knowledge; Context7-MCP was not available in this research session — verify exact signatures at Stage 3 implementation time, especially `juce::AudioPlayHead::getPosition()` and `juce::dsp::Oversampling` re-prepare semantics)
- `juce::dsp::WaveShaper<float>` — core mechanism for nearly all Distortion Engine algorithms via `functionToUse` lambda
- `juce::dsp::Oscillator<float>` — sine/triangle/saw LFO shapes and Ring-Mod carrier
- `juce::dsp::StateVariableTPTFilter<float>` — LP/HP/BP/Resonant LP/Resonant HP (no native Notch — needs `juce::dsp::IIR::Filter` + `makeNotch()`)
- `juce::dsp::DelayLine<float, Lagrange3rd>` — Glitch Engine variable-rate reads, Feedback loop delay, Comb filter
- `juce::dsp::Oversampling<float>` — Quality/qualityMode engine; requires `setLatencySamples()` for PDC
- `juce::dsp::Limiter<float>` — Transparent output limiter mode
- `juce::dsp::BallisticsFilter<float>` — Envelope Follower / Audio Level Mod Matrix sources
- `juce::AudioPlayHead::getPosition()` — JUCE 8 returns `std::optional<PositionInfo>`; older `getCurrentPosition(CurrentPositionInfo&)` pattern is deprecated/removed — used by both Sequencer and tempo-synced LFOs
- `juce::ValueTree` — Sequencer pattern data, custom non-APVTS state
- `juce::SmoothedValue<float>` — XY Pad glide/inertia (the exact mechanism the brief's "smoothing/inertia" requirement calls for), Macro-affected parameter smoothing

### Technical Resources
- DAFX (Digital Audio Effects) — waveshaping/distortion and comb/delay-based effects chapters relevant to Distortion Engine and Filter Stage design
- Standard phase-vocoder/granular-synthesis literature — relevant if Glitch Engine's Granular Repeat mode needs deeper treatment than a simple windowed-grain approach

## Notes

- This architecture treats "Modulation Matrix," "Macros," "Sequencer," and "Performance Triggers" as four layers of the SAME underlying mechanism (a unified per-parameter modulation accumulator) rather than four independent systems, because that's the only way they can coexist without conflicting when multiple sources target the same destination simultaneously — this is the single most important architectural insight from this research pass and should not be re-litigated at Stage 3 without strong reason.
- Several parameter-spec gaps were identified during research and should be resolved (via product decision, not further DSP research) before Stage 3: (1) whether `distortionAlgorithm=Bitcrusher/SampleRateReducer` should actually engage anything beyond the always-on Bitcrush/SRR stage, (2) the feedback loop's internal delay TIME (brief mentions Feedback/Damping/Filter controls but not an explicit delay-time parameter), (3) concrete `qualityMode=AUTO` heuristic, (4) `macroWidth`'s behavior before the post-MVP Stereo module ships.
- Given the deferred UI mockup, `xyPadXTarget`/`xyPadYTarget` "any macro or parameter" routing, per-LFO shape/sync parameters, and Mod Matrix slot parameters are NOT yet in `parameter-spec-draft.md` — they are introduced in this architecture as necessary for the described functionality and should be reconciled into the authoritative parameter spec once the UI mockup work resumes.
